parsed.explanation: No criminal statute reaches trans identity or presentation, and no documented pattern of anti-trans violence against visitors exists — severity-if-outed is therefore low-to-moderate, not custody- or life-threatening. The operative exposures are state threat-framing (2024 cabinet decision and draft policy targeting LGBTQIA+ advocacy/'promotion', a category a visibly trans foreigner cannot cleanly argue away from) and an absence of anti-discrimination law or family-law recourse, in a conservative social climate with PDA avoidance advised. These sit at tiers 2–3: state suspicion-attachment plus thin recourse, but no documented enforcement against trans people, no facility/custody regimes, and documented prosecutorial guidance treating identity-based hostility as an aggravating factor. Rule-of-law quality is mixed; the guidance is untested. Net: reduced risk, a step below the working-protection tier.

entry_documents.interaction: No sourced border or document-practice friction; whether the Marriage Act affects gender markers on ID is unsourced.

investigation_detention_custody.interaction: No arrests, raids or custody-placement practices recorded against trans or LGBT people.

federal_state_facilities.interaction: No facility-access rules (bathrooms, wards, shelters) documented at any level.

care_services.interaction: No evidence on HRT import, refills, or emergency-care treatment of trans visitors.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Cabinet decision and draft national policy target LGBTQIA+ advocacy/'promotion' as contrary to constitutional, Christian and regional values; suspicion attaches to public visibility, and a foreign visitor has no standing to argue the private-conduct distinction.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Prosecution Policy 2003 and Prosecutors Code treat identity-based hostility as a factor toward prosecution; 2011 UN joint statement signed.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Drafting committee's output and enforcement form unsourced; application of prosecutorial guidance undocumented.

minors_guardians.interaction: No age-dependent rules or family/minor-specific exposure recorded.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No documented pattern of anti-trans violence against visitors; conservative climate advises avoiding PDA; only one prosecuted anti-lesbian violence case nationally (2016 record).
street_violence_police_response.protection: Prosecutorial guidance on SGBV and identity-based hostility is the clearest recourse.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Court presence of LGBTI persons near-invisible; guidance application in practice unsourced.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No anti-discrimination protection by orientation or identity; same-sex partners excluded from Family Protection Act 2008 recourse; marriage unavailable and unregistrable.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Harmful Digital Communications Act s2(2)(j) bars orientation-based denigration; Teaching Service Act protects one commission only (resident-facing).
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Whether the advocacy policy was finalised, its legal form, and ID-marker effects are open questions.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar band: sporadic social hostility, no custodial threat, thin remedies. Here the state-level threat-framing (advocacy-ban direction) is somewhat heavier than 0.55-E's contractor-driven ejections, but no transit-police harassment is documented at all.

Slightly below: 0.75-C has trained border officers and a functioning tribunal; here no protective machinery is documented as operating for visitors beyond prosecutorial guidance, and state framing targets the community's visibility.

Clearly above: no universal-exposure measure, no register, no entry exclusion or administrative sanction applies to trans visitors; consequences of outing are social discrimination, not state-sanctioned exclusion or removal.

parsed.synthesis: The combined regime is a no-criminalisation jurisdiction whose traveller-facing record is mostly quiet: no border friction, custody rules, facility bans or violence patterns are documented, and prosecutorial guidance offers real (if untested) recourse against identity-based hostility. The heaviest documented feature is state threat-framing — a 2024 cabinet decision and draft national policy targeting LGBTQIA+ advocacy — which raises discovery stakes for a visibly trans visitor because the 'promotion' category is undefined and the visitor cannot invoke resident protections. Conservative social norms (PDA avoidance, no gay scene, church/chief opposition to advocacy) are friction-to-hostility tier, not enforcement. Open questions (final form of the policy, ID-marker effects, guidance application) are unresolved but not exposures. This places the jurisdiction in Reduced Risk, low in the band.
